original_question: Does the reverse-mathematical strength of either the Halpern-Lauchli Theorem or Milliken's theorem depend on the splitting properties of the underlying finitely branching trees; for example, are binary-branching trees weaker than ternary-branching trees, and are both weaker than trees whose branching is finite but unbounded?
target_in_paper: Section 2, Problem (8): the open problem asking whether the reverse-mathematical strength of the Halpern-Läuchli theorem or Milliken's theorem depends on the trees' splitting properties, with the sample comparisons 2-branching versus 3-branching versus finitely-but-unboundedly branching trees. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1808.10227.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's official formulation: it correctly focuses on reverse-mathematical strength, names the two relevant principles (Halpern-Läuchli and Milliken), and reproduces the paper's own branching comparison examples (binary, ternary, and finite-but-unbounded branching). It also stays narrowly on the tree-splitting issue rather than drifting into neighboring Rado-graph problems. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1808.10227.pdf))
missing_details: The paper is asking this in the reverse-mathematics setting; nearby problems explicitly formulate the comparison over RCA0, so that base theory should be made explicit in a stand-alone version. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1808.10227.pdf))

For Halpern-Läuchli, the nearby context identifies the relevant version as the strong-tree version, and Problem (4) treats the number d of trees as a separate parameter; to isolate branching, d should be held fixed rather than left implicit. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1808.10227.pdf))
For Milliken, the nearby context is Milliken's Ramsey theorem for strong trees on one infinite finitely branching tree with no terminal nodes. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1808.10227.pdf))

For Milliken's theorem, the height of the finite strong trees being colored is another separate parameter, because Problem (7) asks independently whether the strength depends on that height; a sharpened version of Problem (8) should therefore keep height fixed. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1808.10227.pdf))

The phrase splitting properties should be unpacked by naming the exact branching regimes the paper mentions: 2-branching, 3-branching, and finitely but unboundedly branching trees. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1808.10227.pdf))
refined_question: Over RCA0, and holding fixed the non-branching parameters of the principle (for the strong-tree Halpern-Läuchli theorem, a finite number d of trees; for Milliken's Ramsey theorem for strong trees on one infinite finitely branching tree with no terminal nodes, the height of the finite strong trees being colored), does the reverse-mathematical strength of either theorem depend on the splitting properties of the ambient trees? More specifically, are the versions restricted to 2-branching trees weaker than the corresponding versions for 3-branching trees, and are these in turn weaker than the corresponding versions for trees that are finitely branching but have no uniform finite bound on branching? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1808.10227.pdf))
justification: arXiv:1808.10227 is a short problem list rather than a theorem/proposition paper, so there is no Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3 to target here; the nearest official formulation matching your draft is Section 2, Problem (8). The additions in the refined version come from the immediately surrounding context: Section 1 identifies the relevant versions as the Halpern-Läuchli theorem for any finite number of trees and Milliken's theorem for strong trees on one infinite finitely branching tree with no terminal nodes; Problem (1) shows the ambient reverse-mathematics setting is over RCA0; Problem (4) separates the Halpern-Läuchli parameter d; and Problem (7) separates the height parameter for Milliken. No explicitly equivalent reformulation of Problem (8) is proved in the paper. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1808.10227.pdf))
